around.headline: Three LPG cylinders explode in an illegal storage shed near a Bengaluru school
around.summary: Cylinders blew up one after another in an unlicensed storage shed near a school; no casualties were reported, per The Times of India and ThePrint. If you spot cylinders stacked in a residential lane, report it to 112 rather than ignore it.

around.headline: Fake medicine racket: SIT arrests another accused
around.summary: The SIT probing the counterfeit-medicine racket has made a fresh arrest, per The Times of India. Buy from a chemist you trust and check batch number and packaging.

around.headline: Traffic police issue advisory as heavy rain floods roads, brings down a tree in Malleswaram
around.summary: Overnight rain flooded roads, and a traffic cop had to clear a drain on a waterlogged flyover, per The Hindu, Deccan Herald and India Today. More rain is forecast, so leave early and avoid underpasses.

around.headline: New Bengaluru elevated corridors over 10 km to be tolled
around.summary: Moneycontrol reports that the city's upcoming elevated corridors longer than 10 km will carry tolls. Expect a cost trade-off on future commutes.

around.headline: BMRDA notifies mobility road grid; minister sets 15-day deadline to identify critical outskirts roads
around.summary: The road grid for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region is notified, and a 15-day deadline is set for identifying critical roads on the outskirts, per The Hindu and The Times of India. Check the grid before buying or renting on the periphery.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Consumer forum orders hospital to pay Rs 60,000 over unhygienic premium suite
around.summary: A Bengaluru couple paid Rs 1.4 lakh for a premium suite and found cockroaches on food; the hospital was told to pay Rs 60,000, per The Times of India. Keep photos and bills — they are your evidence in consumer court.

around.headline: Rs 3,000 crore of drugs seized from an Iranian boat in the Arabian Sea
around.summary: Five Pakistan nationals were detained in the seizure, per The Hindu. Large drug hauls like this are why police keep warning residents against handling unknown parcels.

street_smart.title: It's peak-hour rain in Bengaluru. Ahead, an underpass is filled with brown water. A few bikes and an SUV are ploughing through and the car behind you is honking. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Hindu / Deccan Herald / India Today: heavy rain floods Bengaluru roads, traffic advisory issued (2026-09-30).
street_smart.situation: You can't tell how deep it is. The alternative is a 15-minute detour and you're already late.

choices.text: Follow the SUV through — if it made it, you will too.
choices.feedback: Depth is hidden under muddy water, and a tall SUV clears what a hatchback or bike can't. Water that gets into the engine air intake causes hydrolock, and stalled vehicles trap occupants when the water keeps rising.

choices.text: Rev hard in first gear and go through quickly to beat the water.
choices.feedback: Speed creates a bow wave that pushes water into the intake and exhaust, and hidden potholes or open drains can wreck the car or throw a rider.

choices.text: Don't enter. Pull over safely, take the detour or wait, and call 112 or the traffic helpline if the underpass is unmarked.
choices.feedback: You can't judge the depth or road condition, so the only safe test is not entering. Ten minutes lost costs far less than a stalled car or a swept-off bike.

choices.text: Walk in first to check the depth, then decide.
choices.feedback: Waterlogged roads hide open manholes, drains and live wires from streetlight or signal poles, so walking in exposes you to those hazards.

takeaways: Never drive or ride through water when you can't see the road surface; when unsure, turn around.
If the engine stalls in water, don't restart it — hydrolock can wreck it. Push it out and call for help.
Report flooded or dangerous stretches to 112 or the Bengaluru traffic police.

quiz.question: What is the reported use of the road grid notified by BMRDA for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region?
options: To prevent congestion as the city expands
quiz.why: BMRDA is the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority, which plans growth beyond the city's municipal limits.

quiz.question: Per today's news, how much was the hospital told to pay the Bengaluru couple over the unhygienic suite?
quiz.why: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, you can file a consumer complaint online through the e-Daakhil portal.

quiz.question: What is happening to Bengaluru's new elevated corridors over 10 km, per Moneycontrol?
quiz.why: Elevated corridors are built above ground to separate through-traffic from local street traffic.

quiz.question: Which Indian state has Bengaluru as its capital?
quiz.why: Karnataka's legislature meets at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru, and the state also holds a session at Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi.

quiz.question: What does LPG, as in the cylinders in today's Bengaluru shed blast, stand for?
quiz.why: LPG is a mix mainly of propane and butane; it's heavier than air, so leaks pool near the floor.
